paragraphs: Morwenna practically vibrated with excitement.
"Captain!" Morwenna volunteered eagerly, stepping forward and drawing the Astral Corsair from its scabbard.
The deep-blue cosmic veins in the metal pulsed violently.
"If we can’t blow it up, let me just walk in there! I can use Tidal-Blade Arts to slash the main tunnel in half! I’ll flood the lower levels with phantom heavy-water!"
Eluned aggressively glared at the pirate.

"You are an unrefined brute!" Eluned insulted her directly. "Did the parameters completely skip over your water-logged brain? If you slash the main support beams, the entire cavern collapses! We lose the loot!"
"At least I’m offering a functional melee solution!" Morwenna bickered back instantly, her feral eyes flashing. "You just want to stand in the back and throw shiny leaves at them!"
"I am an SSS-Rank Goddess!" Eluned shrieked.
"And I am the Dread Queen!" Morwenna roared back.
Silas aggressively pinched the bridge of his nose.
The SSS-Rank kindergarten was officially back in session.
Before Silas could order them to shut up, Tasmin confidently stepped forward into the middle of the bickering divinities.
The Wilderness Huntress drew her chained daggers with the dark crimson flames instantly igniting at the tips.

"My Lord," Tasmin offered with absolute, unyielding loyalty. "I know the exact interior layout... I will gladly run into the darkness, aggro the entire horde, and act as bait to draw them out into the clearing for the Vanguard!"
Total silence fell over the raid team.
Silas looked at Tasmin.
Morwenna looked at Tasmin.
Eluned looked at Tasmin.
Brida and the girls looked at Tasmin.
And then, in perfect coordinated unison, every single person in the group completely ignored her.
Silas turned his attention directly back to the cavern.
Morwenna went back to glaring at Eluned.
Brida adjusted her heavy shield.
Tasmin stood there with her flaming daggers completely useless.
"Hey!" Tasmin complained loudly with her pride taking a massive hit. "I am the fastest unit here! I can easily outrun a Corrupted Orc!"

"Absolutely not," Thora shut the assassin down entirely, stepping forward and dropping her heavy canvas duffel bag into the mud. "You literally got your spine pulverized into sawdust exactly three hours ago. We are not risking you getting grabbed again... Act mature about this."
Tasmin violently puffed her cheeks out, completely humiliated.
’You know it’s bad when Thora is the one being mature...’ Silas thought.
"Besides," Thora grinned, kneeling down and unzipping her heavy duffel bag. "I have the exact perfect tool for this specific tactical scenario."
Thora reached deep into the bag of highly volatile explosives.
She pulled out a small smooth gray sphere.
It was roughly the size of a baseball, completely covered in intricate complex runic engravings that pulsed with a irritating yellow light.
"What the hell is that?" Brida asked, leaning over her shield to inspect the device.

"It’s a Sonic-Aggro Emitter..." Thora explained proudly, tossing the heavy metal sphere casually in her hand. "I completely modified a standard concussive grenade chassis. Instead of exploding outward, the internal runes generate a highly concentrated high-frequency sound wave that physically irritates the eardrums of monsters... It is designed to draw hostile targets out of their defensive hiding places."
Silas stared at the highly advanced snd incredibly specific piece of tactical equipment.
’She literally built a specialized monster-lure grenade from scratch?’ Silas thought, baffled by the speed of her production.
"When exactly did you have the time to completely engineer, design, and forge a custom sonic grenade?" Silas asked, his voice deadpan. "You spent all night forging my armor and other stuff."
Thora shrugged her muscled shoulders with a massive arrogant grin on her face.
"I have a lot of free time, Boss!" Thora laughed loudly.
She didn’t wait for formal authorization.
Thora aggressively cocked her arm back and violently hurled the small gray sphere directly into the pitch-black maw of the cavern.
The metal ball sailed through the air in a perfect flawless arc, disappearing completely into the deep shadows of the tunnel.
Exactly three seconds later, the mechanical latches engaged.
EEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEE!
A condensed shrill agonizing sound wave violently erupted from the depths of the cave.
The high-frequency pitch was completely silent to human ears, but it caused the muddy ground to physically vibrate.
Instantly, the silence of the Umbral Basin was shattered.
ROOOOOOAAAAAAAR!
A massive deafening symphony of guttural, homicidal roars erupted from the darkness.
The sound of dozens of heavy armored footsteps frantically rampaging up the stone tunnel echoed loudly, shaking the ironwood trees.
It wasn’t a small scouting party this time...
It was a whole horde.
"Form a perimeter!" Silas roared, drawing the violently glowing Tier 3 Azure Guillotine from its scabbard. "Do not let them break the line!"
The Vanguard responded instantly.
Brida slammed her heavy kite shield into the mud, planting her boots firmly.
Fenna and Elara knocked arrows, drawing the bowstrings back to their cheeks.
The monsters violently breached the cavern entrance.
It was an terrifying tidal wave of corrupted monsters.
Dozens of towering eight-foot-tall Tier 2 Corrupted Orcs poured out of the cave, wielding heavy rusted iron maces.
They were flanked by a massive pack of Umbral Wolves... massive pitch-black direwolves with glowing red eyes and razor-sharp bone spurs protruding from their spines.
There was a shit ton of them.
"Engage!" Silas ordered.
The clearing instantly erupted into absolute, cinematic violence.
Fenna and Elara didn’t stagger their shots. They engaged a high-speed rapid-fire sequence.
Twang! Twang! Twang!
A massive condensed volley of enchanted arrows rained directly down onto the charging horde.
The arrows didn’t aim for the heavy breastplates.
They found the unarmored gaps in the Orcs’ thick necks and the glowing red eyes of the Umbral Wolves, dropping half a dozen targets before they even crossed the clearing.
"Hold the line!" Brida roared.
A massive mutated Tier 2 Orc completely bypassed the arrows and charged directly at the heavy infantry commander, swinging a heavy iron club.
Brida didn’t flinch as she applied Morwenna’s lesson perfectly.
She didn’t brace her shield flat.
She angled the heavy mythril edge exactly fifteen degrees to the right.
The massive iron club hit the angled shield and deflected harmlessly to the side, completely throwing the Orc off-balance.
Brida aggressively stepped forward, swinging the pulsing axe in a brutal upward arc.
SQUELCH!
The heavy mythril axe entirely, completely bisected the towering Orc from groin to sternum.
Black blood erupted across the mud as the two halves of the monster fell away.
To her right, Gunnhild was putting on a show.
The towering spearwoman utilized a flawless high-speed thrusting technique.
WHOOSH!
She didn’t slash.
She kept her distance, utilizing the massive reach advantage of her heavy spear.
She rapidly pierced the throats of three charging Umbral Wolves in quick succession with her movements looking very fluid.
"Too slow!" Tasmin laughed loudly, she was back in her element.
The Wilderness Huntress flipped gracefully through the air, entirely clearing the front line.
She landed directly on the broad armored shoulders of a confused Orc.
"Die!"
SWISH!
Tasmin crossed her flaming Tier 3 daggers against its neck like a pair of scissors and violently jerked her arms outward.
The Orc’s head cleanly popped off with the stump instantly cauterized by the dark crimson fire.
The girls were dealing work, but the volume of monsters pouring out of the cave was threatening to overwhelm their stamina.
"Allow me..." Eluned sighed politely, stepping forward into the mud.
The Goddess of Nature didn’t draw a weapon.
She didn’t even raise her hands.
She simply looked at the massive horde of charging Orcs, entirely unimpressed by their biology.
Eluned lifted her flawless bare left foot and gently, casually stomped directly down onto the muddy ground.
KRA-KOOM!
The entire clearing violently shook.
A massive surge of pure condensed SSS-Rank nature mana erupted directly into the bedrock beneath the horde.
Instantly, dozens of massive razor-sharp thick ironwood spikes violently erupted completely out of the earth.
They shot upward with terrifying velocity, entirely impaling twenty Corrupted Orcs and a dozen Umbral Wolves simultaneously.
The monsters were skewered mid-stride with their heavy bodies lifted completely off the ground and suspended in the air like grotesque bleeding trophies.
"Show off," Morwenna muttered, deeply annoyed by the massive AoE kill-steal.
The Dread Queen didn’t stay idle.
She completely abandoned the defensive line, charging directly toward a cluster of heavily armored Orcs that had managed to bypass the wooden spikes.
Morwenna didn’t use a standard sword technique...
She swung the Astral Corsair in a wide, sweeping horizontal arc as she engaged her Tidal-Blade Arts at 15% output.
A massive wave of phantom dark blue heavy-water erupted directly from the edge of her blade.
The crushing pressure of the deep-sea slash hit the Orcs like a literal tsunami.
Their heavy iron armor instantly crumpled inward with their ribcages shattering completely under the pressure before the blade even physically touched them.
"Hehehahaha! Don’t you want more?!"
The clearing was a slaughterhouse.
The black mud was completely choked with the mutilated, burning, and skewered corpses of the dungeon horde.
Silas stood in the center of the chaos calmly.
He didn’t swing wildly.
He executed simply clean flawless strikes with The Azure Guillotine, cleanly severing the limbs of any Umbral Wolf that got too close to his backline archers.
The horde was rapidly thinning out as the girls had successfully broken the primary wave.
And then, the heavy earth-shattering sound of massive footsteps echoed from the cave entrance.
Silas instantly locked his golden-ringed eyes onto the yawning darkness.
The ambient air in the clearing violently shifted.
The temperature completely plummeted.
The low-tier monsters still surviving on the field actively flinched and scrambled out of the way.
A massive towering behemoth stepped entirely out of the cavern and into the gray daylight of the Umbral Basin.
It was massive.
It stood an impossible twelve feet tall.
Its thick, leathery hide was a bruised sickly shade of obsidian black as heavy unrefined plates of raw mythril were bolted directly into its collarbones and spine.
It held a massive thick pillar of solid iron ripped directly from a mine cart track and it’s crimson eyes burned with a intelligent sadistic light.
It was the exact monster that Tasmin had described.
"ROOOOOHHHHHH!" the behemoth bellowed as a massive wave of killing intent blasting across the clearing.
It locked its glowing crimson eyes directly onto Silas, instantly recognizing the Mythic Gold Core as the primary alpha threat on the battlefield.
It didn’t hesitate.
It shot forward instead with its massive iron-plated boots tearing huge gouges in the mud.
"RAHHHHH!"
It raised the solid iron pillar high above its head, preparing to completely crush the Sovereign into paste but Silas didn’t back away.
He didn’t ask Morwenna or Eluned to intervene.
This was a very personal execution.
Silas gripped the hilt of The Azure Guillotine tightly in his right hand.
"So you like bullying girls, huh?" Silas muttered with his voice cold and lacking any sort of mercy.
The monster swung the massive iron pillar in a brutal sweeping downward arc.
Silas didn’t block it.

He ignited his Mythic Gold Core to maximum output as a blinding roaring aura of pure golden sovereign mana erupted directly from his body, completely engulfing the Midnight Carapace armor and the blade of his sword.
He stepped directly inside the monster’s massive guard and Silas executed a single overwhelmingly powerful upward slash.
The golden mana condensed entirely along the razor-sharp edge of the cosmic steel.
SHING!
The sound was incredibly crisp.
The Azure Guillotine effortlessly, flawlessly cleaved completely through the solid iron pillar.
It didn’t stop.
The golden blade tore directly upward, slicing cleanly through the thick mythril armor plating on the monster’s chest, slicing through its thick obsidian hide, and passing entirely through its skull.
Silas stood perfectly still with his sword extended high into the air.
For a fraction of a second, the twelve-foot behemoth stood frozen in place.
And then, a massive glowing golden line appeared perfectly down the exact center of its massive body.

chapters.title: Chapter 93: Path To Revenge [IV]
paragraphs: The Tier 3 monster had been completely split entirely in half from the crotch directly to the top of its head in a singular unstoppable upward slash.
The two massive symmetrical halves of the monster completely fell away from each other, crashing heavily into the mud with a deafening sound.
THUD!
Black blood and viscera spilled violently across the clearing as Silas slowly lowered his glowing sword.
He walked casually over to the severed, right half of the monster’s massive head lying in the dirt and he looked down at the dead glazed crimson eye.

’Fucking pathetic... but I guess it’s more pathetic that I almost lost Tasmin over this whole thing.’ Silas thought, he had been holding off but it was about time he started using Upgrade Points to up the ranks of the girls. ’So they can have some variety in moves.’
Silas leaned forward and disrespectfully spat directly onto the monster’s severed face.
It was a cold display of dominance as he had completely avenged his captain.
The Vanguard girls stared in staggering awe.
The overwhelming power of their Sovereign casually one-shotting a Tier 3 monster was terrifyingly magnificent.
"My Lord!" Tasmin shouted excitedly from the back of the formation, running forward through the mud.
Silas turned around, expecting a deeply grateful hug from his woman; however Tasmin stopped a few feet away, looking down at the two halves of the massive, obsidian-skinned Orc lying in the mud.
She frowned slightly as her dark eyes narrowed in genuine confusion.
"That was an incredible strike, my Lord!" Tasmin praised loudly.
She paused, scratching the back of her head.
"But... that wasn’t the one."
Silas froze.
His brain stalled as he looked at Tasmin.
He looked back down at the massive twelve-foot-tall, mythril-plated, obsidian-skinned Tier 3 Orc he had just violently cleaved in half.
"What do you mean, that wasn’t the one?" Silas asked with his voice sounding flat. "You described a massive obsidian-skinned Orc with mythril plating wielding an iron pillar."
"Yes," Tasmin agreed, pointing her dagger at the corpse. "But the one that broke my spine had a massive durning gash straight through its left eye... I blinded it with my flaming dagger."
Silas looked down at the severed head.
Both of its massive crimson eyes were completely intact.
There were no burn marks.
The realization hit Silas like a physical, highly kinetic blow to the chest.
’If this massive, heavily armored, twelve-foot-tall Tier 3 behemoth wasn’t the actual Boss...’ Silas thought with a sigh. ’Then what the hell did I just kill?’
"O-oh..." Silas muttered out loud.
The blood-soaked clearing outside the cavern entrance was finally growing quiet.
The deafening high-frequency mechanical ringing from Thora’s specialized sonic-aggro grenade had finally faded into a dull echo, completely running out of internal mana.
The massive horde of Corrupted Orcs and Umbral Wolves that had poured out of the depths had been entirely reduced to a sprawling carpet of butchered burning meat.
There were no more monsters rushing out of the pitch-black maw of the cave.
Tasmin was currently finishing the job.
She stood over a massive armored Tier 2 Orc that was desperately trying to crawl back toward the safety of the tunnel with its legs entirely paralyzed by a gravity crush from Rowena.
Tasmin didn’t waste any energy.
She smoothly stepped onto the center of the monster’s broad, mythril-plated back, pinning it to the mud.
With a sharp fluid flick of her wrist, she drove her dark iron dagger directly into the narrow, unarmored gap at the base of the Orc’s thick neck.
SQUELCH!
The super-heated dark crimson tip of the blade effortlessly severed the brain stem.
The massive monster instantly went limp with its corrupted yellow eyes rolling completely back into its skull.
Tasmin retracted her chain, the burning flames instantly extinguishing as she cut the mana flow.
She wiped a streak of black corrosive blood from her pale cheek and turned around to face the formation.
"Target rich environment completely cleared, my Lord," Tasmin reported sharply, seamlessly falling back into her professional stance.
She walked over to where Silas was standing, wiping her blades on a piece of ruined canvas.

"However," Tasmin added with her dark eyes narrowing as she looked back at the carnage. "I can confirm with certainty that these specific Orcs were significantly weaker and more disorganized than the ones my group originally faced."
She pointed one of her daggers directly toward the dark yawning cavern entrance.
"They fought like terrified, mindless grunts," Tasmin concluded. "The one that actually attacked me... the massive behemoth with the missing eye. It is still inside and it didn’t take the bait."
Silas didn’t argue with her assessment as he thinned his lips into a tight line.
He reached down and smoothly sheathed The Azure Guillotine.
The terrifying cosmic blue hum of the Tier 3 blade vanished the exact second the steel slid into the dark leather scabbard at his hip.
"Understood," Silas stated coldly with his golden-ringed eyes completely locked onto the dark tunnel. "Girls... Reform the perimeter. We are going inside."
The heavily armed girls of the squad didn’t hesitate.
Brida hoisted the violently pulsing axe onto her shoulder, Fenna knocked a fresh arrow to her bow, and the entire group seamlessly shifted into a tight flawless diamond formation.
As they began marching across the muddy clearing, a heavy weight suddenly dropped directly onto Silas’s right shoulder.
"Let’s go spelunking, Boss!" a loud, abrasive voice cheered right next to his ear.
Silas didn’t even break his stride.
He let out a long exhausted sigh.
Thora, the half-naked Dwarven blacksmith, had casually climbed up his massive, armored frame like he was a designated jungle gym.
She was currently sitting completely behind his neck with her thick bare legs aggressively wrapped entirely around his shoulders.
"Do you absolutely have to ride me like a bipedal tactical mount?" Silas asked deadpan. "Why did you also have to come out half-naked? You exhibitionist..."

"It’s the safest spot on the entire battlefield!" Thora laughed unapologetically, pulling another highly mechanical gadget out of her heavy canvas duffel bag. "Besides, your new Tier 3 armor has excellent lumbar support."
They breached the threshold of the cavern.
The transition was instant and jarring like when Tasmin had entered.
The gray, ash-choked daylight of the Umbral Basin completely vanished, swallowed entirely by the oppressive blackness of the deep-earth mining tunnel.
The sound of the freezing monsoon rain faded into a dull distant hum. In the center of the formation, Rowena stepped forward.
The elegant human mage raised her violently glowing Sapphire-Core World Weaver high into the air.
"Visibility is currently compromised," Rowena stated smoothly with her melodic voice echoing off the stone walls. "My Lord, Allow me to cast a sustained fire rune to illuminate the—"
"Absolutely the fuck not!" Thora instantly interrupted from her perch on Silas’s shoulder.
The Dwarven blacksmith aggressively pointed a soot-stained finger down at the academic mage.

"Do not cast raw magic in an unventilated high-density mining tunnel, you amateur!" Thora scolded her. "If there are pocketed veins of volatile mana-gas or highly pressurized deep-earth dust hanging in the ambient air, your little fire rune will completely ignite the entire cavern! You’ll turn us all into a meat geyser before we even see the main thing!"
Rowena immediately froze mid-incantation.
Her pale face flushed a deep explosive shade of crimson at the harsh professional reprimand.
She quickly lowered her staff as she was humiliated.
’I’ll get back at you for this... fucking dwarf.’
"I have the exact ttool for this," Thora bragged loudly.
She held up the mechanical gadget she had just pulled from her bag.
It looked like a heavy brass torch, heavily modified with intricate Dwarven gears and glowing blue runes etched directly into the metal casing.
Thora didn’t just light it.
She tapped a specific runic sequence on the side of the handle and casually tossed the heavy brass torch directly into the empty air above the Vanguard.
The torch didn’t fall to the ground.
It buzzed violently and began to perfectly float exactly three feet above the formation.
FWOOSH.
The internal runes ignited, generating a brilliant bright white light that instantly flooded the entire cavern tunnel.
It completely pushed the heavy darkness away, revealing every single microscopic detail of the surrounding stone walls.
"An anti-gravitational cold-light emitter," Thora explained proudly, crossing her arms over her chest. "It’s completely non-thermal and hands-free which is perfect lighting for deep-vein operations."
The bright white light revealed a staggering mind-numbing fortune.
The jagged obsidian walls of the tunnel were literally bursting with raw valuable unmined mythic ores.
Massive veins of glowing blue star-iron, dark deep-earth alloy, and highly condensed mana crystals glittered brilliantly under the cold light but Thora wasn’t looking at the basic mythril.
Her keen Master Smith eyes instantly locked onto a very specific rare anomaly protruding from the stone wall exactly ten feet ahead.
"By the Ancestors!" Thora gasped loudly, her eyes going completely wide with scientific obsession.
She didn’t ask for permission as she violently launched herself entirely off Silas’s shoulders.
Thora sailed through the air and landed heavily against the rough stone wall.
She grabbed onto a massive, jagged, violently pulsing, deep-crimson crystal that was protruding thickly from the rock face.
The crystal was incredibly dense.
It looked like a chunk of frozen blood.
"I need to extract this immediately for metallurgical testing!" Thora babbled with her face pressed against the glowing rock.
She planted her heavy, iron-plated boots firmly against the obsidian wall for leverage.
She gripped the massive crimson crystal with both of her leather-gloved hands and violently, aggressively yanked backward with all of her raw Dwarven might.
The crystal didn’t budge.
It was firmly rooted deep within the bedrock.
Thora didn’t give up.
She aggressively threw her entire body weight backward as she repeatedly yanked on the crystal frantically.
"Come on... you... stubborn... piece of... junk!" Thora grunted loudly.
With every single violent pull, her bare Dwarven ass shook excessively, jiggling wildly in the bright white light of the floating lantern.
The Vanguard girls completely froze.

They stared at the ridiculous undignified spectacle of the territory’s Master Smith aggressively twerking against a rock wall while grunting like a degenerate but then again... That behavior was not above her
"Is she serious right now?" Brida whispered, aggressively rubbing her temples beneath her helmet.
"It’s completely stuck!" Thora complained loudly while panting heavily.
She turned her head to look back at the formation with a shameless expression.
"Boss! A little assistance over here? I need to study the internal matrix of this crystal!"
Silas stood in the center of the tunnel.
’I am running an army of lunatics man...’ Silas thought as he accepted his fate with a deep sense of exhaustion.
Silas smoothly drew The Azure Guillotine from its scabbard.
With a single and precise flick of his wrist, Silas casually whipped the Tier 3 cosmic blade in a downward arc.
A wave of golden sovereign mana shot across the tunnel as the mythic edge cleanly severed the base of the crimson crystal directly where it connected to the obsidian wall.
Thora, who was still actively pulling backward with all of her body weight, instantly lost all structural leverage.
"Whoa!" Thora yelped.
She violently flew backward through the empty air, entirely out of control.
She hit the hard stone floorboards with a splat, landing squarely on her bare ass.
The massive, severed crimson crystal landed perfectly into her lap.
"Ow," Thora grumbled, rubbing her bruised tailbone but her annoyance vanished instantly the second she looked down at the pulsing gemstone resting against her thighs.

"I have absolutely never seen this specific crystalline structure before in my entire life," Thora muttered with her eyes completely glazed over. "The internal mana density is incredibly unstable... I will be sure to research the exact properties of this one back at the Foundry."
She quickly stuffed the massive crystal entirely into her heavy duffel bag, zipped it shut, and scrambled back up to her feet.
She didn’t stay on the ground.
She immediately climbed right back up Silas’s armored frame, seamlessly resuming her bipedal mount position on his shoulders.
As Silas sheathed his sword and continued walking deeper into the tunnel, the two SSS-Rank entities of his squad smoothly stepped up to flank him.
Morwenna matched his pace on the right with her hand resting casually on the hilt of the Astral Corsair.
Eluned floated silently on his left with her glowing green eyes completely focused on the dark path ahead.
In perfect coincidental unison, both women turned their heads to look directly at him.
"Captain, I have a guess about—" Morwenna started smoothly.
"My Lord, I have a very strong suspicion regarding—" Eluned started at the exact same microsecond.

sentences.text: The Tier 3 monster had been completely split entirely in half from the crotch directly to the top of its head in a singular unstoppable upward slash.
The two massive symmetrical halves of the monster completely fell away from each other, crashing heavily into the mud with a deafening sound.
THUD!
Black blood and viscera spilled violently across the clearing as Silas slowly lowered his glowing sword.
He walked casually over to the severed, right half of the monster’s massive head lying in the dirt and he looked down at the dead glazed crimson eye.

’Fucking pathetic... but I guess it’s more pathetic that I almost lost Tasmin over this whole thing.’ Silas thought, he had been holding off but it was about time he started using Upgrade Points to up the ranks of the girls. ’So they can have some variety in moves.’
Silas leaned forward and disrespectfully spat directly onto the monster’s severed face.
It was a cold display of dominance as he had completely avenged his captain.
The Vanguard girls stared in staggering awe.
The overwhelming power of their Sovereign casually one-shotting a Tier 3 monster was terrifyingly magnificent.
"My Lord!" Tasmin shouted excitedly from the back of the formation, running forward through the mud.
Silas turned around, expecting a deeply grateful hug from his woman; however Tasmin stopped a few feet away, looking down at the two halves of the massive, obsidian-skinned Orc lying in the mud.
She frowned slightly as her dark eyes narrowed in genuine confusion.
"That was an incredible strike, my Lord!" Tasmin praised loudly.
She paused, scratching the back of her head.
"But... that wasn’t the one."
Silas froze.
His brain stalled as he looked at Tasmin.
He looked back down at the massive twelve-foot-tall, mythril-plated, obsidian-skinned Tier 3 Orc he had just violently cleaved in half.
"What do you mean, that wasn’t the one?" Silas asked with his voice sounding flat.
"You described a massive obsidian-skinned Orc with mythril plating wielding an iron pillar."
"Yes," Tasmin agreed, pointing her dagger at the corpse.
"But the one that broke my spine had a massive durning gash straight through its left eye...
I blinded it with my flaming dagger."
Silas looked down at the severed head.
Both of its massive crimson eyes were completely intact.
There were no burn marks.
The realization hit Silas like a physical, highly kinetic blow to the chest.
’If this massive, heavily armored, twelve-foot-tall Tier 3 behemoth wasn’t the actual Boss...’ Silas thought with a sigh. ’Then what the hell did I just kill?’
"O-oh..." Silas muttered out loud.
The blood-soaked clearing outside the cavern entrance was finally growing quiet.
The deafening high-frequency mechanical ringing from Thora’s specialized sonic-aggro grenade had finally faded into a dull echo, completely running out of internal mana.
The massive horde of Corrupted Orcs and Umbral Wolves that had poured out of the depths had been entirely reduced to a sprawling carpet of butchered burning meat.
There were no more monsters rushing out of the pitch-black maw of the cave.
Tasmin was currently finishing the job.
She stood over a massive armored Tier 2 Orc that was desperately trying to crawl back toward the safety of the tunnel with its legs entirely paralyzed by a gravity crush from Rowena.
Tasmin didn’t waste any energy.
She smoothly stepped onto the center of the monster’s broad, mythril-plated back, pinning it to the mud.
With a sharp fluid flick of her wrist, she drove her dark iron dagger directly into the narrow, unarmored gap at the base of the Orc’s thick neck.
SQUELCH!
The super-heated dark crimson tip of the blade effortlessly severed the brain stem.
The massive monster instantly went limp with its corrupted yellow eyes rolling completely back into its skull.
Tasmin retracted her chain, the burning flames instantly extinguishing as she cut the mana flow.
She wiped a streak of black corrosive blood from her pale cheek and turned around to face the formation.
"Target rich environment completely cleared, my Lord," Tasmin reported sharply, seamlessly falling back into her professional stance.
She walked over to where Silas was standing, wiping her blades on a piece of ruined canvas.
"However," Tasmin added with her dark eyes narrowing as she looked back at the carnage.
"I can confirm with certainty that these specific Orcs were significantly weaker and more disorganized than the ones my group originally faced."
She pointed one of her daggers directly toward the dark yawning cavern entrance.
"They fought like terrified, mindless grunts," Tasmin concluded.
"The one that actually attacked me... the massive behemoth with the missing eye.
It is still inside and it didn’t take the bait."
Silas didn’t argue with her assessment as he thinned his lips into a tight line.
He reached down and smoothly sheathed The Azure Guillotine.
The terrifying cosmic blue hum of the Tier 3 blade vanished the exact second the steel slid into the dark leather scabbard at his hip.
"Understood," Silas stated coldly with his golden-ringed eyes completely locked onto the dark tunnel.
"Girls...
Reform the perimeter.
We are going inside."
The heavily armed girls of the squad didn’t hesitate.
Brida hoisted the violently pulsing axe onto her shoulder, Fenna knocked a fresh arrow to her bow, and the entire group seamlessly shifted into a tight flawless diamond formation.
As they began marching across the muddy clearing, a heavy weight suddenly dropped directly onto Silas’s right shoulder.
"Let’s go spelunking, Boss!" a loud, abrasive voice cheered right next to his ear.
Silas didn’t even break his stride.
He let out a long exhausted sigh.
Thora, the half-naked Dwarven blacksmith, had casually climbed up his massive, armored frame like he was a designated jungle gym.
She was currently sitting completely behind his neck with her thick bare legs aggressively wrapped entirely around his shoulders.
"Do you absolutely have to ride me like a bipedal tactical mount?" Silas asked deadpan.
"Why did you also have to come out half-naked?
You exhibitionist..."
"It’s the safest spot on the entire battlefield!" Thora laughed unapologetically, pulling another highly mechanical gadget out of her heavy canvas duffel bag.
"Besides, your new Tier 3 armor has excellent lumbar support."
They breached the threshold of the cavern.
The transition was instant and jarring like when Tasmin had entered.
The gray, ash-choked daylight of the Umbral Basin completely vanished, swallowed entirely by the oppressive blackness of the deep-earth mining tunnel.
The sound of the freezing monsoon rain faded into a dull distant hum.
In the center of the formation, Rowena stepped forward.
The elegant human mage raised her violently glowing Sapphire-Core World Weaver high into the air.
"Visibility is currently compromised," Rowena stated smoothly with her melodic voice echoing off the stone walls.
"My Lord, Allow me to cast a sustained fire rune to illuminate the—"
"Absolutely the fuck not!" Thora instantly interrupted from her perch on Silas’s shoulder.
The Dwarven blacksmith aggressively pointed a soot-stained finger down at the academic mage.
"Do not cast raw magic in an unventilated high-density mining tunnel, you amateur!" Thora scolded her.
"If there are pocketed veins of volatile mana-gas or highly pressurized deep-earth dust hanging in the ambient air, your little fire rune will completely ignite the entire cavern!
You’ll turn us all into a meat geyser before we even see the main thing!"
Rowena immediately froze mid-incantation.
Her pale face flushed a deep explosive shade of crimson at the harsh professional reprimand.
She quickly lowered her staff as she was humiliated.
’I’ll get back at you for this... fucking dwarf.’
"I have the exact ttool for this," Thora bragged loudly.
She held up the mechanical gadget she had just pulled from her bag.
It looked like a heavy brass torch, heavily modified with intricate Dwarven gears and glowing blue runes etched directly into the metal casing.
Thora didn’t just light it.
She tapped a specific runic sequence on the side of the handle and casually tossed the heavy brass torch directly into the empty air above the Vanguard.
The torch didn’t fall to the ground.
It buzzed violently and began to perfectly float exactly three feet above the formation.
FWOOSH.
The internal runes ignited, generating a brilliant bright white light that instantly flooded the entire cavern tunnel.
It completely pushed the heavy darkness away, revealing every single microscopic detail of the surrounding stone walls.
"An anti-gravitational cold-light emitter," Thora explained proudly, crossing her arms over her chest.
"It’s completely non-thermal and hands-free which is perfect lighting for deep-vein operations."
The bright white light revealed a staggering mind-numbing fortune.
The jagged obsidian walls of the tunnel were literally bursting with raw valuable unmined mythic ores.
Massive veins of glowing blue star-iron, dark deep-earth alloy, and highly condensed mana crystals glittered brilliantly under the cold light but Thora wasn’t looking at the basic mythril.
Her keen Master Smith eyes instantly locked onto a very specific rare anomaly protruding from the stone wall exactly ten feet ahead.

The crystal was incredibly dense.
It looked like a chunk of frozen blood.

chapters.title: Chapter 94: Path To Revenge [V]
paragraphs: They both stopped speaking immediately as they slowly turned their heads glaring violently at each other across Silas’s armored chest.
"Do not completely interrupt my debrief, you overgrown weed..." Morwenna snarled with her feral gray eyes narrowing dangerously.
"I am his primary woman, you washed-up trench-rat!" Eluned shrieked back territorially. "I speak to him first! It is my right!"
"I will literally wrap my anchor chain entirely around your neck and drag you into the—"
"I will turn your blood into aggressive flesh-eating thorns before you even draw—"
Silas aggressively raised his hand, completely chopping the impending catastrophic SSS-Rank argument in half.
"I am begging you," Silas sighed. "Just tell me exactly what the problem is before my brain physically hemorrhages."
Morwenna and Eluned both huffed, aggressively crossing their arms over their chests and looking away from each other.

"The behaviors of the low-tier monsters we just slaughtered outside were very strange, Captain," Morwenna reported first with their instincts taking over. "Orcs and Wolves are aggressive territorial apex predators but they didn’t fight like they wanted to kill us."
She frowned, looking down at the dark stone floor.
"They fought like they were terrified," Morwenna concluded. "Like they were actively fleeing from something much worse, and we were simply in their way."
"The trench-rat is actually correct," Eluned agreed reluctantly with her glowing green eyes narrowing in disgust.
The Goddess of Nature raised her delicate hand, summoning a tiny orb of pure green mana.

"When I skewered the horde with my ironwood spikes, I analyzed their internal systems," Eluned explained smoothly. "The monsters were being completely controlled against their actual will. There was a parasitic corrupted seed violently constricting directly around their hearts."
Eluned’s face twisted into a mask of pure divine hatred.

"The entire Dungeon Boss ecosystem in this grid is highly likely to be a massive, parasitic monster that fundamentally relies on the hijacked corrupted power of Nature to control its subordinates..." Eluned stated coldly.
She clenched her fist, crushing the glowing green orb of mana.
"And for that exact reason," Eluned hissed, her voice vibrating with true divine wrath. "I completely hate it. It defiles my domain."
Silas didn’t argue with her.
He knew Eluned was a Goddess of Nature at her core.
Anything that actively corrupted the natural order of biology was a direct personal insult to her divine authority.
"Understood," Silas nodded grimly. "Stay on high alert... The main chamber should be just—"
RUMBLE!
The solid stone floor beneath their boots violently shifted.
It wasn’t a distant earthquake. It was a direct ambush on their location.
The thick smooth obsidian floorboards exactly ten yards ahead of the group formation physically exploded outward.
Massive chunks of heavy rock and compressed dirt shot violently into the air, bouncing off the ceiling.
From the freshly created craters, massive horrors erupted entirely out of the ground.
They were colossal armored Umbral Spiders. They were easily the size of armored cavalry horses, covered in thick, dark purple carapace plates that looked like solid iron.
Their eight compound eyes burned with a sickly corrupted yellow light, and their massive venom-dripping mandibles clicked aggressively in the cold light of Thora’s lantern.
There were easily two dozen of them, completely blocking the tunnel and chittering loudly.
"Ambush!" Tasmin yelled, drawing her chained daggers.
"I have the crowd control!" Rowena shouted enthusiastically from the center of the formation.
The elegant human mage stepped forward, raising the violently pulsing Sapphire-Core World Weaver high into the air.
She didn’t hesitate.
She began rapidly channeling her maximum mana output into the mythic staff, fully preparing to drop a massive, crushing gravity well directly onto the spider horde.
"Mage, halt your cast!" Morwenna barked sharply.
The Dread Queen stepped forward, grabbing Rowena’s arm to interrupt the spell.
Rowena blinked, entirely confused. "But they are swarming the bottleneck!"

"Do not entirely waste your energy reserves on disposable trash mobs!" Morwenna scolded the mage smoothly. "You have a massive mana pool, but it is not infinite! Save your high-yield crowd control for the actual Parasite!"
Morwenna didn’t fall back into the formation.
The SSS-Rank Pirate Queen stepped directly to the absolute front of the Vanguard line.
She didn’t draw her heavy boarding anchor as she casually rested her right hand on the hilt of the Astral Corsair.
She turned her head, looking over her shoulder directly at Silas.
"Captain," Morwenna requested with a confident grin stretching across her pale face. "Do not waste your energy... Let me clear the deck."
Silas didn’t argue.
He crossed his arms over his armored chest and nodded. "Show them how it’s done, Morwenna."
The massive horde of Umbral Spiders shrieked with their mandibles clicking wildly as they charged forward.
Their heavy armored legs skittering terrifyingly across the stone floor as they moved with unnatural speed, preparing to overwhelm the single woman standing in their path.
Morwenna didn’t wait for them to close the distance.
She smoothly drew the Astral Corsair and the cosmic deep-blue veins etched into the Tier 3 mythril blade flared violently to life.
She fluidly dropped her center of gravity as she engaged her Tidal-Blade Arts at 20% output.
Morwenna executed a single horizontal slash.
VWOOSH!
She didn’t just generate a small wave of phantom water.
A massive wide crescent arc of dark blue deep-ocean water completely erupted from the edge of her blade.
The crushing pressure of the slash entirely filled the width of the mining tunnel, scraping against the stone walls.
The dark blue arc shot forward with staggering velocity as it hit the charging horde of Umbral Spiders like a tsunami.
The attack didn’t just cut them.
The atmospheric pressure of the heavy-water entirely crushed their thick purple carapaces inward.
The blade of phantom water passed completely through the entire horde in a fraction of a second, tearing through their dense body as if they were made of wet paper.
The tunnel went dead silent and then, every single one of the twenty-four massive Umbral Spiders completely fell apart.
They had been flawlessly split in half horizontally.
Black spider blood, corrupted viscera, and toxic venom flooded the stone floor in a massive tidal wave of gore.
Morwenna calmly, fluidly sheathed the Astral Corsair. The entire execution had taken exactly one point five seconds.
The Vanguard girls stared at the carnage in awe as Rowena slowly lowered her mythic staff, realizing exactly how far the gap in their martial power truly was.
Silas stood behind the Dread Queen, deeply impressed by the flawless display of kinetic violence.
"That was cool," Silas complimented her genuinely with his deep voice echoing in the quiet tunnel.
Morwenna physically froze.
The terrifying SSS-Rank mythic entity who had just casually bisected two dozen giant armored spiders completely lost her feral swagger.
Her pale cheeks instantly flushed a bright, undeniable shade of crimson. She looked down at her boots with a small flustered giddy smile touching her lips.
’The Captain thinks my swordplay is cool!’ Morwenna thought as her face melted. ’I am definitely getting that promotion!’
"Move up," Silas ordered smoothly, breaking her out of her stupor.
The girls advanced deeper into the cavern, carefully stepping entirely over the bisected bleeding corpses of the spider horde.
As they walked, the physical environment of the tunnel began to drastically, visibly change.
The smooth carved obsidian rock walls began to warp.
The glowing valuable veins of blue star-iron and deep-earth alloy were no longer pristine as they were being violently overrun.
Massive corrupted white roots were violently spreading across the walls, the floor, and the ceiling.
The roots were actively burying themselves deep into the mythic ores, draining the ambient mana from the crystals like giant leeches.
The stale smell of the mine entirely vanished.
It was instantly replaced by a thick and overwhelmingly sickeningly sweet scent. It smelled like rotting fruit mixed with highly concentrated cloying sugar.
Silas’s Gold Core combat instincts violently flared.
The hairs on the back of his neck stood completely straight up.
"Stay on absolute guard..." Silas ordered sharply with his hand resting entirely on his sword hilt. "That scent is an active neurotoxin. The Boss is trying to pacify us."
Eluned didn’t tolerate the insult.
The Goddess of Nature aggressively stepped forward. Her glowing green eyes narrowed in pure disgust at the corrupted flora choking the stone walls.
She lifted her bare foot and violently stamped it directly onto the root-covered floor.
KRA-KOOM!
A massive overwhelming wave of pure pristine nature mana violently erupted from her body.

The sickeningly sweet scent was entirely obliterated as the heavy and fresh dominating scent of ancient pines, morning dew, and blooming wildflowers completely flooded the tunnel, forcefully suppressing the Boss’s neurotoxin.
"Pathetic corrupted garbage," Eluned cursed the white roots, glaring at them in absolute disgust. "I will burn this entire root system to ash."
Sitting safely on Silas’s shoulder, Thora finally realized the truth of the situation.
The Dwarven blacksmith pulled the massive, severed crimson crystal completely out of her duffel bag.
She held it up to the bright white light of the floating lantern, inspecting the internal matrix as they walked past the corrupted roots.
"I understand why this specific crystal is crimson!" Thora gasped loudly, her eyes wide with sheer, scientific revelation.
"Why?" Silas asked, keeping his eyes entirely on the path ahead.

"It’s not just a standard mythic ore!" Thora explained frantically, tapping the glowing red crystal. "It is a crystallization of condensed monster blood completely fused with the ambient deep-earth alloy! The corrupted roots are actively bleeding the monsters into the rock! This is amazing! It’s a living biological metal!"
Before Thora could completely nerd out over the discovery, the tunnel abruptly ended.
They stepped entirely out of the narrow corridor and into the absolute main chamber of the dungeon.
The room was massively wide. It was a sprawling subterranean cavern easily the size of a modern football stadium and the ceiling was entirely lost in the dark shadows high above.
The entire floor of the cavern was completely, entirely packed with hostile targets.
There were a lot of of them.

Corrupted Orcs, massive Umbral Spiders, and heavily mutated Dire-Wolves filled every available square inch of the muddy ground and standing directly in the center of the horde, towering entirely over the rest, was the massive, twelve-foot-tall Tier 3 Behemoth Orc that had mangled Tasmin.
Its left eye was a ruined charred crater of burned flesh, matching Tasmin’s exact report but none of the monsters were actively charging and none of them were roaring.
Every single monster in the massive cavern was currently kneeling.
They were completely bowed in terrified submission, facing the far end of the stadium-sized room.
Rooted deeply into the bedrock at the back of the cavern was a massive, towering, heavily corrupted tree.
Its bark was a sickly necrotic gray as its sprawling twisted branches were completely covered in heavy glowing white petals that actively pulsed with the sickeningly sweet toxic mana.
The tree didn’t have a face... It didn’t speak...
But Silas could physically feel the massive spike in the ambient atmospheric pressure.
He felt the terrifying psychic command completely issue forth directly from the roots of the tree, broadcasting straight into his Mythic Gold Core.
It was a silent order to slaughter the intruders.
In perfect unison, every single kneeling monster in the massive cavern slowly turned their heads.
Dozens of glowing corrupted yellow and crimson eyes locked entirely onto the squad standing in the tunnel entrance.
Silas didn’t flinch.
He slowly drew The Azure Guillotine.
The cosmic blue Tier 3 mythic blade hummed with violent golden authority.
He took a deep breath, preparing to issue the command to his army.
"Atta—" Silas started to yell, raising his sword high into the air.
He didn’t even get to finish the word.
A blur of dark leather and spinning iron chains violently shot past him.
"On it!" Tasmin shrieked happily, completely abandoning formation and launching herself into the air directly toward the blinded Tier 3 Behemoth that had broken her spine.

The massive horde of Umbral Spiders shrieked with their mandibles clicking wildly as they charged forward.
Their heavy armored legs skittering terrifyingly across the stone floor as they moved with unnatural speed, preparing to overwhelm the single woman standing in their path.
Morwenna didn’t wait for them to close the distance.
She smoothly drew the Astral Corsair and the cosmic deep-blue veins etched into the Tier 3 mythril blade flared violently to life.
She fluidly dropped her center of gravity as she engaged her Tidal-Blade Arts at 20% output.
Morwenna executed a single horizontal slash.
VWOOSH!
She didn’t just generate a small wave of phantom water.
A massive wide crescent arc of dark blue deep-ocean water completely erupted from the edge of her blade.
The crushing pressure of the slash entirely filled the width of the mining tunnel, scraping against the stone walls.
The dark blue arc shot forward with staggering velocity as it hit the charging horde of Umbral Spiders like a tsunami.
The attack didn’t just cut them.
The atmospheric pressure of the heavy-water entirely crushed their thick purple carapaces inward.
The blade of phantom water passed completely through the entire horde in a fraction of a second, tearing through their dense body as if they were made of wet paper.
The tunnel went dead silent and then, every single one of the twenty-four massive Umbral Spiders completely fell apart.
They had been flawlessly split in half horizontally.
Black spider blood, corrupted viscera, and toxic venom flooded the stone floor in a massive tidal wave of gore.
Morwenna calmly, fluidly sheathed the Astral Corsair.
The entire execution had taken exactly one point five seconds.
The Vanguard girls stared at the carnage in awe as Rowena slowly lowered her mythic staff, realizing exactly how far the gap in their martial power truly was.
Silas stood behind the Dread Queen, deeply impressed by the flawless display of kinetic violence.
"That was cool," Silas complimented her genuinely with his deep voice echoing in the quiet tunnel.
Morwenna physically froze.
The terrifying SSS-Rank mythic entity who had just casually bisected two dozen giant armored spiders completely lost her feral swagger.
Her pale cheeks instantly flushed a bright, undeniable shade of crimson.
She looked down at her boots with a small flustered giddy smile touching her lips.
’The Captain thinks my swordplay is cool!’ Morwenna thought as her face melted. ’I am definitely getting that promotion!’
"Move up," Silas ordered smoothly, breaking her out of her stupor.
The girls advanced deeper into the cavern, carefully stepping entirely over the bisected bleeding corpses of the spider horde.
As they walked, the physical environment of the tunnel began to drastically, visibly change.
The smooth carved obsidian rock walls began to warp.
The glowing valuable veins of blue star-iron and deep-earth alloy were no longer pristine as they were being violently overrun.
Massive corrupted white roots were violently spreading across the walls, the floor, and the ceiling.
The roots were actively burying themselves deep into the mythic ores, draining the ambient mana from the crystals like giant leeches.
The stale smell of the mine entirely vanished.
It was instantly replaced by a thick and overwhelmingly sickeningly sweet scent.
It smelled like rotting fruit mixed with highly concentrated cloying sugar.
Silas’s Gold Core combat instincts violently flared.
The hairs on the back of his neck stood completely straight up.
"Stay on absolute guard..." Silas ordered sharply with his hand resting entirely on his sword hilt.
"That scent is an active neurotoxin.
The Boss is trying to pacify us."
Eluned didn’t tolerate the insult.
The Goddess of Nature aggressively stepped forward.
Her glowing green eyes narrowed in pure disgust at the corrupted flora choking the stone walls.
She lifted her bare foot and violently stamped it directly onto the root-covered floor.
KRA-KOOM!
A massive overwhelming wave of pure pristine nature mana violently erupted from her body.

The sickeningly sweet scent was entirely obliterated as the heavy and fresh dominating scent of ancient pines, morning dew, and blooming wildflowers completely flooded the tunnel, forcefully suppressing the Boss’s neurotoxin.
"Pathetic corrupted garbage," Eluned cursed the white roots, glaring at them in absolute disgust.
"I will burn this entire root system to ash."
Sitting safely on Silas’s shoulder, Thora finally realized the truth of the situation.
The Dwarven blacksmith pulled the massive, severed crimson crystal completely out of her duffel bag.
She held it up to the bright white light of the floating lantern, inspecting the internal matrix as they walked past the corrupted roots.
"I understand why this specific crystal is crimson!" Thora gasped loudly, her eyes wide with sheer, scientific revelation.
"Why?" Silas asked, keeping his eyes entirely on the path ahead.
"It’s not just a standard mythic ore!" Thora explained frantically, tapping the glowing red crystal.
"It is a crystallization of condensed monster blood completely fused with the ambient deep-earth alloy!
The corrupted roots are actively bleeding the monsters into the rock!
This is amazing!
It’s a living biological metal!"
Before Thora could completely nerd out over the discovery, the tunnel abruptly ended.
They stepped entirely out of the narrow corridor and into the absolute main chamber of the dungeon.
The room was massively wide.
It was a sprawling subterranean cavern easily the size of a modern football stadium and the ceiling was entirely lost in the dark shadows high above.
The entire floor of the cavern was completely, entirely packed with hostile targets.
There were a lot of of them.

Corrupted Orcs, massive Umbral Spiders, and heavily mutated Dire-Wolves filled every available square inch of the muddy ground and standing directly in the center of the horde, towering entirely over the rest, was the massive, twelve-foot-tall Tier 3 Behemoth Orc that had mangled Tasmin.
Its left eye was a ruined charred crater of burned flesh, matching Tasmin’s exact report but none of the monsters were actively charging and none of them were roaring.
Every single monster in the massive cavern was currently kneeling.
They were completely bowed in terrified submission, facing the far end of the stadium-sized room.
Rooted deeply into the bedrock at the back of the cavern was a massive, towering, heavily corrupted tree.
Its bark was a sickly necrotic gray as its sprawling twisted branches were completely covered in heavy glowing white petals that actively pulsed with the sickeningly sweet toxic mana.
The tree didn’t have a face...
It didn’t speak...
But Silas could physically feel the massive spike in the ambient atmospheric pressure.
He felt the terrifying psychic command completely issue forth directly from the roots of the tree, broadcasting straight into his Mythic Gold Core.
It was a silent order to slaughter the intruders.
In perfect unison, every single kneeling monster in the massive cavern slowly turned their heads.
Dozens of glowing corrupted yellow and crimson eyes locked entirely onto the squad standing in the tunnel entrance.
Silas didn’t flinch.
He slowly drew The Azure Guillotine.
The cosmic blue Tier 3 mythic blade hummed with violent golden authority.
He took a deep breath, preparing to issue the command to his army.
"Atta—" Silas started to yell, raising his sword high into the air.
He didn’t even get to finish the word.
A blur of dark leather and spinning iron chains violently shot past him.
"On it!" Tasmin shrieked happily, completely abandoning formation and launching herself into the air directly toward the blinded Tier 3 Behemoth that had broken her spine.

chapters.title: Chapter 95: A Tier 4 Monster!
paragraphs: She didn’t wait for orders.
A second blinding blur of emerald green magic violently shot past his other shoulder.

"Wait entirely for me!" Eluned yelled competitively, actively summoning a massive ironwood staff and charging directly into the center of the horde. "I am going to completely uproot that disgusting weed!"
"Don’t you dare kill the Boss before I get there, Goddess!" Morwenna roared, sprinting directly into the mud, her Astral Corsair leaving a trail of blue cosmic light.
"For the Blessed Land!" Brida bellowed, hoisting the axe and charging into the fray.
Fenna, Maren, Hilda, Gunnhild, and Elara completely abandoned the disciplined diamond formation.
They entirely broke ranks, screaming battle cries and eagerly charging head-first directly into the massive stadium of heavily armored monsters.
They were bloodthirsty and they didn’t want to hold a defensive line.
They wanted to slaughter...
Silas stood completely alone in the tunnel entrance, his sword raised for a command that nobody had stayed around to listen to.
’I can’t even be mad at them...’ Silas thought with a sigh but he didn’t look angry.
He slowly lowered his glowing blade with an affectionate proud smile touching his lips.
"Don’t entirely worry, my Lord!" a loud abrasive voice cheered from high above.
Silas looked up.
Thora was still sitting securely on his shoulders with her thick thighs completely wrapped around his neck. She patted the top of his head affectionately.
"I’d absolutely never leave yo—" Thora started to promise her complete loyalty.
Silas didn’t hesitate.
He calmly reached up, grabbed the Dwarven blacksmith by the back of her heavy helmet, and forcefully threw her off his shoulders and directly into the middle of the raging battlefield.
"AGGGGHHHH!" Thora screamed as she sailed through the air toward a pack of Umbral Wolves.
Silas smirked, adjusting his armor in the cold light of the floating lantern.
"Clear the room," Silas ordered the empty air.
"AGGGGHHHH!"
Thora’s scream echoed violently across the cavern.
The half-naked Dwarven blacksmith sailed completely through the air, flailing her muscled limbs as she plummeted directly toward a massive snarling pack of Umbral Wolves.
The wolves didn’t hesitate.
They were corrupted predators.

Seeing a chunk of raw unarmored meat literally falling out of the sky and directly into their kill zone, five of the massive dire-wolves leaped simultaneously into the air with their venom-dripping jaws unhinging to rip her apart before she even hit the ground.
They entirely underestimated the territory’s Master Smith.
Thora’s terrified screaming stopped the exact microsecond she was in striking range.
Her panic completely vanished, instantly replaced by a massive grin.
"Just kidding, you ugly mutts!" Thora cackled loudly.
She reached behind her back and she didn’t pull out a heavy forging hammer.
With a sharp ring, she drew a pristine and perfectly balanced custom-forged shortsword.
The blade wasn’t made of standard iron.
It was forged from a hyper-conductive variant of deep-earth alloy, and the flat of the metal was completely covered in glowing blue runes.
Thora forcefully surged her mana directly into the hilt.
KRACK-THOOM!
A blinding deafening explosion of pure high-voltage lightning violently erupted directly from the blade.
The lightning didn’t just shock them.
It arced aggressively through the damp, humid air of the cavern, instantly chaining between all five airborne Umbral Wolves.
The electrical voltage completely flash-fried their internal nervous systems.
Their corrupted yellow eyes violently burst.
Their dark fur instantly caught fire, filling the air with the sickening stench of charred meat and Thora landed heavily in the mud, rolling perfectly to absorb her momentum.
The five charred, smoking wolf corpses crashed to the ground around her, completely dead before they even hit the dirt.
"I call this one The Defibrillator!" Thora laughed maniacally, raising her crackling, lightning-wreathed shortsword. "Who else wants a shock therapy session?!"
She aggressively charged entirely into the horde, swinging her lightning blade like an absolute lunatic.
Behind her, the rest of the Vanguard was dealing work.
They had entirely abandoned their defensive diamond formation, turning the massive subterranean cavern into a slaughterhouse.
Brida was an unstoppable tank.
The towering commander waded directly into the thickest cluster of Corrupted Orcs.
The purple gravity runes on the axe pulsed violently with every single swing.
She wasn’t just cutting monsters... she was actively manipulating the physical mass of her strikes.
"Come get some fuckers!"
She swung the massive battleaxe in a brutal sweeping horizontal arc, cleanly bisecting three armored Orcs at the waist.
Their heavy top halves slid off their legs with black blood geysering into the mud.
Gunnhild was a maestro of lethal distance.
The spearwoman utilized her heavy shaft to perfectly control the engagement zone.
An Umbral Spider leaped at her from a rocky outcropping, its mandibles clicking wildly but Gunnhild didn’t step back.
She planted her back foot and thrust her spear upward with terrifying velocity.
The heavy iron spearhead punched cleanly through the spider’s thick purple carapace, completely skewering its vital organs and pinning it to the cavern ceiling.
Fenna and Elara didn’t stop firing.
The two archers had found a high-ground vantage point on top of a massive boulder of unmined ore.
They operated with terrifying precision. Every time an arrow left their bowstrings, a monster’s skull violently snapped backward.
And Tasmin was a complete blur of dark crimson fire.
The Wilderness Huntress was actively hunting.
She completely utilized Morwenna’s lesson, condensing the thermal output of her daggers strictly to the razor-sharp tips.
She danced through the chaotic melee with her chains whipping through the air.
She didn’t waste a single drop of excess mana as every strike was perfect.
She severed hamstrings, melted through iron breastplates, and instantly dropped targets with ruthless efficiency.
The girls were winning but Silas wasn’t looking at the trash mobs.
His golden-ringed eyes were completely locked onto the massive twelve-foot-tall armored Behemoth standing in the center of the stadium-sized room.
The massive Orc wielded its solid iron mine-cart pillar. Its left eye was a ruined blackened crater of cooked flesh.

Silas completely ignored the chaotic fighting happening around him as he marched directly through the battlefield. A cold suffocating aura of pure sovereign killing intent rolling off his Midnight Carapace armor.
"Tasmin," Silas called out, his deep voice effortlessly cutting through the sounds of slaughter.
Tasmin decapitated a wolf and landed gracefully on the mud, looking over her shoulder.
"Is that the one?" Silas asked flatly, pointing The Azure Guillotine directly at the scarred behemoth.
Tasmin looked at the towering monster. Her dark eyes flashed with pure spite.
"Yes, my Lord," Tasmin confirmed sharply. "That is the exact bastard that pulverized my spine."
Silas didn’t say another word... He didn’t need to...
BANG!
Silas exploded forward.
His heavy iron-plated boots violently cracked the obsidian floorboards, instantly propelling his massive Gold Core frame across the fifty-yard distance.
The Tier 3 Behemoth instantly recognized the approaching threat and the massive monster didn’t just rely on its raw physical mass.
It actually possessed a mana core.
The Orc roared, heavily channeling a massive surge of corrupted, dark-purple earth mana entirely into its solid iron pillar.
The crude weapon instantly doubled in size, completely coated in a thick layer of volatile bedrock.
It swung the massive mana-enhanced pillar in a brutal sweeping downward arc designed to completely flatten Silas into the mud but Silas didn’t dodge.
He wanted to make a very painful point.

Silas stopped his forward momentum entirely and he smoothly raised The Azure Guillotine with a single hand, catching the descending multi-ton iron pillar perfectly on the cosmic blue edge of his blade.
KRA-KOOM!
The impact was apocalyptic.
The force of the clash instantly generated a massive gust of wind.

The shockwave aggressively exploded outward, blowing the remaining low-tier monsters entirely off their feet and tearing the heavy white petals off the corrupted tree at the back of the room but Silas didn’t budge a single millimeter.
His boots sank two inches deep into the solid bedrock.
His Mythic Gold Core flared violently, effortlessly absorbing the crushing weight.
The Behemoth’s remaining crimson eye went completely wide in terror.
It pushed down with all of its massive, twelve-foot-tall muscular strength, but the human standing beneath the pillar simply refused to move.
Silas didn’t just hold the block.
He didn’t try to use fluid technique or elegant redirection like Morwenna either... partly because he couldn’t do it.
Regardless, he was a warlord, and he fought with overwhelming brute force.
He violently surged his Mythic Gold Core, channeling a massive explosive pulse of pure mass directly into his arms.
With a brutal earth-shattering shove, Silas applied leverage to the edge of his cosmic sword.
He aggressively batted the multi-ton weapon entirely to the side with pure crushing strength.
The rebound ripped the monster’s massive leathery hands entirely off the iron shaft.
The Behemoth violently stumbled forward, completely losing its balance and over-committing to the broken strike as its guard was fatally exposed.
"This is for Tasmin..." Silas whispered coldly.
He didn’t swing with elegant finesse.
He executed a brutal horizontal cleave, fueled entirely by golden sovereign mana.
The Tier 3 cosmic blade tore through the ambient air with a deafening roar.
It completely bypassed the monster’s heavily armored mythril breastplate, targeting the unarmored gap directly beneath its massive chin.
SHING!
The weight of the cut was so incredibly violent that there was virtually zero physical resistance.
Silas smoothly followed through with the slash, stepping neatly past the stumbling behemoth.
He smoothly sheathed The Azure Guillotine as he walked away, never looking back.
The massive Tier 3 Boss stood entirely frozen for a fraction of a second and then, its massive, ugly head cleanly slid off its shoulders.
The head hit the mud with a wet thud, immediately followed by the rest of the colossal, twelve-foot body collapsing like a felled tree.
Black, corrosive blood aggressively geysered from the severed stump of its neck, flooding the stone floor.
Silas had just casually parried and decapitated a Dungeon Boss without breaking a sweat but the fight wasn’t completely over.
The exact second the massive Behemoth’s head hit the floor, the entire cavern violently shuddered.
The massive corrupted tree rooted at the back of the room didn’t just sit there.
The death of its primary enforcer completely triggered its automated defense mechanisms as the tree went absolutely berserk.
Its massive necrotic gray trunk physically twisted.
Thousands of thick, violently glowing white roots aggressively erupted entirely out of the mud and the obsidian walls.
They moved with terrifying whip-like velocity.
SWISH! SWISH! SWISH!
Dozens of razor-sharp roots shot directly through the air toward Silas, moving like fired javelins.
Silas didn’t panic as his Gold Core combat instincts engaged instantly.
He fluidly ducked under the first root, side-stepped the second, and casually batted the third away with his armored gauntlet.
He back-stepped smoothly, completely creating a ten-yard tactical buffer zone between himself and the thrashing homicidal flora.
He looked directly at the massive tree and instantly, a glowing blue holographic interface materialized directly in his retinas.
[Target Identified: The Necro-Arbor Sovereign]
[Classification: Tier 4 Boss]

[Description: A massive armored biomechanical terror born from dense necrotic sludge and mana anomalies. Boasts extreme physical density, resistance, and the ability to hijack local biological systems. It is capable of widespread AoE parasitic infection.]
"Tier 4?!" Silas muttered out loud, genuinely, completely surprised by the scaling jump.
He had expected a strong Tier 3 core.
A Tier 4 anomaly located this close to his territory walls was a massive threat as the structural density of a Tier 4 meant standard attacks would practically bounce off its bark.
Before Silas could draw his blade again to deal with the escalated threat, the ambient air directly in front of him completely warped.
Eluned stepped smoothly into his peripheral vision.
The Goddess of Nature didn’t draw a weapon.
She simply stood directly in front of Silas, physically shielding him from the thrashing aggressive roots.
"How dare you!" Eluned hissed as her voice vibrated with divine wrath.
She didn’t cast a complex spell.
She simply spread her slender arms wide, projecting her pure SSS-Rank nature energy completely outward.
The effect was instantaneous and completely overwhelming.
The moment Eluned’s divine aura clashed with the corrupted necrotic mana of the Tier 4 Boss, the entire cavern froze.
